<RuleLanguageLinks current="html" languages={[{"id":"html","label":"HTML","href":"/linter/rules/no-vue-child-content/html/"}]} />

:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueChildContent`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/no-child-content`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/no-child-content)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueChildContent": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow content inside elements whose content is replaced by `v-html` or `v-text`.

The `v-html` and `v-text` directives replace everything between the opening and closing
tags of their element. Vue discards anything written there, including text, other
elements, and comments, so it never appears on the page.

Either remove the content, or remove the directive and keep the content.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <div v-html="html">Loading...</div>
</template>
```

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <div v-html="html"></div>
  <p v-text="message" />
  <div v-html="html">
  </div>
  <div>Loading...</div>
</template>
```

## Options

### `additionalDirectives`

Other directives that replace the content of their element, such as the `v-t` directive
of Vue I18n. Write the names without the `v-` prefix. `v-html` and `v-text` are always
checked.

Default: `[]`

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueChildContent": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"additionalDirectives": [
							"t"
						]
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <p v-t="'greeting'">Hello</p>
</template>
```
